hypotheses.text: The primary clinical and molecular discovery of Cornelia de Lange syndrome 6 (CdLS6) belongs to Olley et al. 2018 in Nature Genetics indexed under PMID 29379197, whereas PMID 30054598 represents an erratum/author correction that contains no original patient phenotyping data.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolving the citation conflict between PMID 29379197 and PMID 30054598 is necessary to establish provenance and assess whether the reported clinical frequencies (4/4 developmental delay, 4/4 microcephaly, 4/4 synophrys) stem from the original primary investigation rather than amendment notes.

evidence.text: The primary paper 'BRD4 interacts with NIPBL and BRD4 is mutated in a Cornelia de Lange-like syndrome' by Olley et al. is cataloged under PMID 29379197 and Nature Genetics, explicitly noting that an amendment has been published.

evidence.text: OMIM entry 620568 and MalaCards reference the original 2018 Olley et al. Nature Genetics discovery under PMID 29379197 as the establishing authority for CDLS6.

hypotheses.text: BRD4-associated CdLS exhibits variant-class divergence, where de novo missense variants affecting chromatin interaction domains produce a facial gestalt indistinguishable from classical CdLS, whereas whole-gene deletions or haploinsufficiency variants produce an atypical, non-classic CdLS-like phenotype.
hypotheses.rationale: Conflicting interpretations exist regarding whether CdLS6 presents uniformly as classic CdLS or non-classic CdLS. Distinguishing the clinical presentations of missense point variants from truncating/deletion variants tests the basis for diagnostic scoring and clinical distinction.

evidence.text: Olley et al. 2018 observed that more typical CdLS presentation occurred with a de novo BRD4 missense variant, whereas general BRD4 haploinsufficiency produced an overlapping but distinct syndrome.

evidence.text: Alesi et al. (2019) documented that BRD4 missense mutations correlate with a typical Cornelia de Lange phenotype, while 19p13 microdeletions causing haploinsufficiency result in an atypical or contiguous gene deletion phenotype.

evidence.text: Lonardo et al. 2025 classify CDLS6 caused by BRD4 alterations comprehensively as non-classic CdLS, underscoring broad clinical variability and milder phenotypes.

source.title: Non-Classic Cornelia de Lange Syndrome Due to BRD4 Gene Alterations: A Literature Review
source.quote: Pathogenic variations in several other genes, including BRD4, have been identified as causative factors for non-classic or milder forms of the syndrome.

hypotheses.text: The reported 100% frequencies for microcephaly (HP:0000252) and synophrys/arched eyebrows (HP:0000664) are specific to intragenic BRD4 point mutant cohorts and drop significantly when 19p13.12 microdeletion patients are included in CdLS6 cohorts.
hypotheses.rationale: Substantiating exact numerator/denominator phenotypic ratios requires segregating isolated BRD4 single-nucleotide variants from contiguous gene deletion patients who harbor multigene haploinsufficiencies.

evidence.text: Alesi et al. (2019) reviewed 19p13.12p13.11 microdeletion cases spanning BRD4 alongside GIPC1, NOTCH3, AKAP8, and CASP14, finding that they share some features of BRD4 point mutation carriers but result in a more complex, atypical presentation.

source.title: Confirmation of BRD4 haploinsufficiency role in Cornelia de Lange–like phenotype and delineation of a 19p13.12p13.11 gene contiguous syndrome
source.quote: Patients harboring a 19p interstitial deletion shared some physical features with BRD4 mutation carriers, which results in a more complex phenotype because of the involvement of several neighboring genes.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact patient-by-patient numerator and denominator counts for synophrys, microcephaly, growth failure, and limb defects across all published CdLS6 individuals with molecularly isolated BRD4 point mutations versus contiguous 19p13.12 deletions?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifies whether the 4/4 and 3/4 phenotypic ratios reported in Olley et al. 2018 hold across larger international series and removes distortion from multi-gene deletion cases.

new_directions.question_text: Do functional alterations in the extra-terminal (ET) domain of BRD4 produce different dysmorphic and neurodevelopmental outcomes compared to alterations in the bromodomains (BD1/BD2)?
new_directions.rationale: NIPBL interacts physically with the BRD4 ET domain (Luna 2019), whereas chromatin binding relies on BD1/BD2 bromodomains, suggesting domain-specific pathomechanisms could drive distinct clinical sub-phenotypes.
